question: Which of the following Acts was passed by Governor General Lord William Bentinck in 1829?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bengal Sati Regulation Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bengal Sati Regulation Act was passed by Governor-General Lord William Bentinck in 1829.
 
• This Act made the practice of Sati illegal and punishable by the courts.
 
• Sati was a practice where a widow immolated herself on her husband's funeral pyre.
 
• The regulation was a significant step towards social reform in British India.
 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy, a prominent social reformer, was instrumental in campaigning against the practice of Sati.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord William Bentinck**

 
 
• Served as the Governor-General of India from 1828 to 1835.
 
• Known for his progressive policies and social reforms.
 
• Also abolished the practice of Thuggee and human sacrifices.
 
 
 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy**
 
 
• A key figure in the Bengal Renaissance and a social reformer.
 
• Founded the Brahmo Samaj in 1828 to promote monotheism and social reform.
 
• Worked tirelessly against social evils like Sati, child marriage, and caste discrimination.
 
 
 
• **Sati Practice**
 
 
• An ancient Hindu funeral custom where a widow self-immolates on her husband's pyre.
 
• Considered as an act of ultimate devotion and purity by some.
 
• Widely condemned and opposed by social reformers and later, the British authorities.
 
 
 
• **Brahmo Samaj**
 
 
• A socio-religious reform movement founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy.
 
• Advocated for the eradication of social evils and the establishment of a more rational and ethical society.
 
• Played a significant role in the 19th-century Bengal Renaissance.
